skill.name: vercel-optimize
skill.description: Audits deployed Vercel projects with production metrics, scoped code analysis, deterministic gates, and verified recommendations for reducing cost and improving route performance.
skill.summary: Find metric-backed Vercel cost and performance improvements.
skill.author: vercel-labs

security_audit.summary: The 400 static alerts are lexical false positives from documentation, regular-expression APIs, relative imports, and constrained Vercel tooling. Two semantic issues remain: model-controlled verifier claims can escape the repository root and can supply unbounded regular expressions. The skill also intentionally reads project source and invokes the authenticated Vercel CLI, so users should review its access before running it. Static review was capped at 400/1603 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 1203 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Verifier file paths and repo roots can be controlled by recommendation claims.
remediation.suggestion: Ignore claim-supplied repoRoot values, reject absolute paths, canonicalize every candidate path, and require it to remain inside the configured repository root and brief allowlist.

remediation.issue: Verifier regular expressions are accepted from model-generated claims without resource limits.
remediation.suggestion: Reject embedded regular-expression literals, cap pattern and file sizes, prefer escaped literal matching, and use a safe-regex check or isolated worker timeout.

semantic_findings.title: Model-Controlled Claims Can Escape the Repository Root
semantic_findings.description: Recommendation output can supply file and repoRoot values that become verifier claims. The path resolver accepts absolute paths and does not verify that normalized relative paths remain under the audited repository.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The data flow is direct: model-provided verifiableClaims retain an optional repoRoot, while repoPaths explicitly accepts absolute files and unchecked joined paths.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Model-Supplied Regular Expressions
semantic_findings.description: Recommendation output can add verifiable claims with arbitrary regular expressions. The verifier compiles and applies them to repository files without length, syntax, or complexity limits, enabling denial of service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The verifier accepts model-provided claim objects, constructs RegExp instances from their patterns, and runs them against file content without resource controls.

content.user_title: Optimize Vercel Cost and Route Performance
content.value_statement: Vercel costs and slow routes are difficult to prioritize without production evidence. This skill combines account metrics, scoped code checks, and verified documentation into ranked recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Collects Vercel metrics, usage, contract, project configuration, and framework details.
Ranks route, project, and account candidates with deterministic thresholds.
Maps supported framework routes to relevant source files for focused investigation.
Checks caching, function duration, errors, cold starts, transfer, builds, and Core Web Vitals.
Validates recommendation claims, file references, project facts, and version-aware citations.
Renders a ranked Markdown report and a concise final message.
limitations: Requires a deployed, authenticated, and linked Vercel project with meaningful traffic.
Observability Plus is required for full route-level analysis and ranking.
Framework coverage is strongest for Next.js and SvelteKit, with narrower Nuxt and Astro support.
It reports opportunities but does not guarantee exact savings or performance gains.

use_cases.title: Reduce a growing Vercel bill
use_cases.description: Identify the billing services, routes, and configurations responsible for observed spend, then rank actionable changes.

use_cases.title: Diagnose slow production routes
use_cases.description: Connect route latency, errors, cold starts, and external API delays to focused source investigations.

use_cases.title: Prepare a platform optimization review
use_cases.description: Assess caching, transfer, builds, bot traffic, and project settings before a capacity or architecture review.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this linked Vercel project. Collect production signals first, then report the highest-confidence cost and performance opportunities.
prompt_templates.scenario: A first audit of a deployed project

prompt_templates.title: Investigate expensive routes
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate slow and expensive routes in this Vercel project. Rank findings by observed impact and cite the responsible files and applicable documentation.
prompt_templates.scenario: A project with rising function usage or latency

prompt_templates.title: Find safe caching opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Find safe caching opportunities for public routes. Exclude authentication, errors, previews, webhooks, mutations, and user-specific responses unless evidence proves caching is safe.
prompt_templates.scenario: A project with low cache efficiency

prompt_templates.title: Run an expanded verified audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the full Vercel Optimize pipeline with a 12-candidate budget. Reconcile deep-dive evidence, verify every claim, and render the final report.
prompt_templates.scenario: A detailed platform and application review

output_examples.input: A Next.js storefront has rising Vercel costs and slow product routes.
output: Prioritize the product API because its traffic and 95th percentile duration dominate observed function usage.
Cache only the public success response, with a named freshness window and verified invalidation.
Keep authenticated and error responses dynamic.

output_examples.input: A content site has poor cache efficiency and high data transfer.
output: Rank high-traffic routes with low cache hit rates.
Identify oversized public assets and image delivery opportunities.
Separate verified recommendations from investigated items that need no change.

best_practices: Run the skill from the intended linked project directory and confirm the Vercel account scope.
Collect production signals before inspecting route source files.
Review cache safety, framework version, and cited evidence before implementing recommendations.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill for projects that are not deployed on Vercel.
Do not infer route impact from code patterns without production traffic evidence.
Do not cache authenticated, error, preview, webhook, mutation, or user-specific responses without proof.

faq.question: Does this skill require a Vercel deployment?
faq.answer: Yes. It is designed for linked Vercel projects with production traffic and authenticated CLI access.

faq.question: Is Observability Plus required?
faq.answer: It is required for full route-level metrics. Without it, the skill asks before continuing with a limited code-only audit.

faq.question: Which frameworks are supported?
faq.answer: Next.js and SvelteKit have the strongest support. Nuxt is supported, Astro is limited, and unknown frameworks pause for confirmation.

faq.question: What data does the skill access?
faq.answer: It reads Vercel metrics, usage, contract, project configuration, linkage identifiers, and relevant local project source files.

faq.question: Does the skill change application code?
faq.answer: The workflow produces recommendations and evidence. Code changes require a separate user-approved implementation step.

faq.question: Will the report provide exact savings?
faq.answer: No. It uses observed performance values and cost magnitude ranges instead of unsupported exact savings estimates.
